paper.title: A simulation study of sample size for multilevel logistic regression models
paper.citation: Moineddin R, Matheson FI, Glazier RH. A simulation study of sample size for multilevel logistic regression models. BMC Medical Research Methodology 7:34 (2007)

simulation.what: The fitted model estimates the covariance σ01 of the random intercept and slope (the model of equation 1), started at 0, although the data are drawn with σ01 = 0. The paper reports no σ01 and does not say whether it was fitted.
simulation.sensitivity: Fitted without σ01 (variant nocov, replicates 0-199 of every cell), {h_nocov_table1_converged} of 27 Table 1 convergence cells come back (mean gap {h_nocov_gap} points), against {h_baseline_table1_converged} (gap {h_baseline_gap} points) with it: without σ01 nearly every data set of groups of 5 converges.

simulation.what: σ0 and σ1 in Tables 1-5 are the variances as fitted (NLMIXED's random statement takes variances): % bias of the variance estimate, Wald interval on the variance. The tables label them σ0 and σ1.
simulation.sensitivity: On the SD scale (bias of the square root, delta-method interval) {h_sd_scale_table1_lowconv} of 48 Table 1 low-convergence cells and {h_sd_scale_table1_stable} of 114 high-convergence cells come back, against {h_main_run_table1_lowconv} and {h_main_run_table1_stable}.

simulation.what: The paper's 'absolute value for parameter convergence criterion' of 1e-8 is read as NLMIXED's ABSXCONV: a fit also counts as converged when no parameter moves by more than 1e-8 in an iteration, which is how fits that creep towards a zero variance stop.
simulation.sensitivity: Without that criterion (variant noabsx, replicates 0-199) {h_noabsx_table1_converged} of 27 convergence cells come back (mean gap {h_noabsx_gap} points).

simulation.what: NLMIXED's dual quasi-Newton is emulated by BFGS with a backtracking (Armijo) line search, an initial Hessian from finite differences, the quadrature re-centred at every iteration, NLMIXED's default ABSGCONV 1e-5 and GCONV 1e-8, 200 iterations and 500 function calls (MAXFUNC). NLMIXED's own line search and update are not public.
simulation.sensitivity: With 2,000 function calls (variant maxfunc2000) {h_maxfunc2000_table1_converged} of 27 convergence cells come back (mean gap {h_maxfunc2000_gap} points).

simulation.what: Quadrature points per dimension chosen at the starting values by NLMIXED's sequence 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 21, 31 with QTOL 1e-4, keeping the larger of the two counts that agree. In our runs: {qpoints} fits used each number of points.
simulation.sensitivity: Keeping the smaller count (variant qfirst): {h_qfirst_table1_converged} of 27 convergence and {h_qfirst_table1_stable} of 114 high-convergence bias cells; 1 point (Laplace, variant q1): {h_q1_table1_converged} and {h_q1_table1_stable}; 3 points (q3): {h_q3_table1_converged} and {h_q3_table1_stable}.

simulation.what: Random numbers: NumPy PCG64, one stream per data set (seed 19554471, study, cell, replicate); the paper's SAS generator and seeds are not given.
simulation.sensitivity: A second run with other seeds (base 19554472): {table1_stable_second} of 114, {table1_lowconv_second} of 48 and {table3_stable_second} of 114 cells within tolerance of the paper.

table4.what: Table 4 pools the nine groups x size cells of the main grid, 1,000 data sets each, at each prevalence; the paper says only that it 'repeated our simulations'.
table4.sensitivity: Pooling only the cells of group size 5: {h_table4_size5_cells_table4} of 54 cells within tolerance; only the cells of 30 groups: {h_table4_groups30_cells_table4}; all nine: {table4_within}. % converged pooled over all nine: {t4_conv_all_cells}; over size 5: {t4_conv_size5} (paper 77, 86, 87).

table5.what: The true variance of a random effect in Table 5 is the variance of the distribution it is drawn from (N(0, 4): 4; U(-2, 2): 4/3; t3: 3; t5: 5/3); the paper does not say.
table5.sensitivity: A wrong truth moves every σ bias of the model by a fixed factor; the t3 models (6 and 7) are the ones whose σ biases miss.

table5.what: Table 5's non-coverage is a share of all 100 data sets of a cell, a data set that did not converge counted as not covered (Tables 3 and 4 take it over converged fits).
table5.sensitivity: Over converged fits only, {h_table5_noncoverage_converged_only_table5_noncoverage} of 432 non-coverage cells come back ({h_table5_noncoverage_converged_only_group_size_5} of 144 at group size 5), against {table5_noncoverage_within} ({h_table5_noncoverage_converged_only_main_run_group_size_5}).

table2.what: Table 2's p-values: a likelihood-ratio test of the 3-level factor in a logistic regression of the non-coverage indicator of every converged fit; compared as significant or not at 0.05.
table2.sensitivity: The paper does not say how the factor entered the model.

exceptions.evidence: sqrt(2.0) = 1.414, which prints as 1.41; the paper prints 1.42 (Methods). The other two σ0 and the three ICCs follow from the stated variances.

readme.details:
## Comparing Monte Carlo tables

No printed cell can come back exactly: the paper's seeds and random-number generator are not given. Each cell is
compared at a tolerance fixed before the comparison: half a unit of the last printed digit plus 3 x √2 Monte Carlo
standard errors of one estimate (ours stands in for the paper's): the SD of the converged fits' estimates over √n
for % bias, √(p(1 - p)/n) for non-coverage and % converged. Table 2's p-values are compared as significant or not at
0.05.

How good is that test? Our second run (other seeds) falls within the tolerance of our main run in
{table1_stable_replicate} of 114, {table1_lowconv_replicate} of 48 and {table1_converged_replicate} of 27 Table 1 cells, and
{table3_stable_replicate} of 114 and {table3_lowconv_replicate} of 48 Table 3 cells. Against the paper, the right designs
give {table1_stable_within} of 114 high-convergence bias cells; the neighbouring design of a wrong input gives at most
{table1_stable_ctrl_max} (a neighbouring ICC barely moves the fixed effects, so only the σ columns and the other factors
tell designs apart), and {table1_converged_ctrl_max} of 27 convergence cells against our {table1_converged_within}. For Table 5
the next model scores {table5_bias_ctrl} bias and {table5_noncoverage_ctrl} non-coverage cells against our
{table5_bias_within} and {table5_noncoverage_within}.

The settings the paper does not state were found by scoring alternatives on the same data sets
(`hypotheses` in `output/comparison.json`): σ01 estimated, the variance scale of σ0 and σ1, the paper's ABSXCONV,
the number of quadrature points, the interval for the variances, Table 4's designs and Table 5's non-coverage.
Each is an assumption of `results.json` with its sensitivity. The variants refit replicates 0-199 of every cell of
the main grid; their records are not kept (about 4 MB), their summaries are (`output/records/extra.json`).

## Layout

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `main.nf`, `nextflow.config` | The pipeline. |
| `requirements.txt` | Pinned Python packages; the package `mlagq` is installed from `../package`. |
| `results_notes.json` | Labels, assumptions, causes and the page's prose, written by hand; merged with the run into `../results.json`. Numbers in the prose are filled from the run. |
| `results.json` | The repository's results check (`tools/check_results.py`): our value for every compared cell and claim. |
| `pipeline/` | `fetch_inputs.sh`, `extract_published.py`, `simulate.py`, `sim_check.py`, `summarize.py`, `record_tests.py`, `compare.py`, `claims.py`, `crosscheck.py`, `build_results.py`, `make_results_check.py`, `build_page.py` with `page_template.html`, `check_reproduction.py`, `update_readmes.py`, `env_versions.py`; copies of the skill's `check_results.py`, `compare_runs.py` and `check_package.py`. |
| `output/published_values.json` | Every printed number of Tables 1-5. |
| `output/records/` | One record per data set (status, estimates, standard errors) of the main grid (27,000), the prevalence study (27,000) and Table 5 (7,200), gzipped CSV with 8 significant digits; `extra.json`, the summaries of the second run and the variants. |
| `output/simulation.json` | Every summary the comparison uses. |
| `output/comparison.json`, `output/tables.csv` | Every printed cell against ours, with tolerances, the second run, the controls and the hypotheses; the same cells as one CSV. |
| `output/claims.json`, `output/record_tests.json` | Every claim of the text against the paper's own tables and our two runs; the tests the claims need from the records (the non-converged follow-up, Shapiro-Wilk, the Table 5 tests). |
| `output/crosscheck.json`, `output/sim_check.json`, `output/package.json` | The likelihood against direct integration; the first replicates rerun from scratch; the package check. |

## Run

```bash
pip install -r PMC1955447/figure-reproduction/requirements.txt ./PMC1955447/package
nextflow run PMC1955447/figure-reproduction/main.nf --outdir results
nextflow run PMC1955447/figure-reproduction/main.nf --outdir results --full       # rerun the whole study
nextflow run PMC1955447/figure-reproduction/main.nf --outdir results --extract    # reread the printed tables from the XML
```

The default run takes about 10 minutes on 4 cores: 378 data sets (the first 3 of every cell) simulated and fitted
again from scratch and checked against the committed records, the summaries, comparisons and claims recomputed
from the records, the cross-check (about 2 minutes) and the package check (about 1 minute). `--full` reruns all
61,200 data sets of Tables 1-5, the second run of Tables 1-3 (27,000) and the six variants (32,400), about 6 CPU
hours. `.github/workflows/reproduce-pmc1955447.yml` runs the default on every pull request that touches this paper,
and `--full` when started by hand.

## Pipeline steps

1. `FETCH`: the article XML from PMC's open-access bucket (Europe PMC as a fallback), SHA-256 checked.
2. `PUBLISHED_VALUES`: the committed printed values, or with `--extract` read again from the XML and checked against them.
3. `RECORDS_COMMITTED` and `SIM_CHECK` (default), or `SIMULATE` (`--full`): the per-replicate records.
4. `SUMMARIZE`: every printed quantity from the records.
5. `RECORD_TESTS`: the non-converged follow-up (refits), Shapiro-Wilk tests and the Table 5 tests.
6. `COMPARE` and `CLAIMS`: every printed cell and claim against ours, the controls and the hypotheses.
7. `CROSSCHECK`: mlagq's likelihood against a dense-grid integral, and its maxima against the exact likelihood's.
8. `PACKAGE`: `check_package.py` on `../package` (wheel, fresh install, tests, tutorial rerun).
9. `RESULTS`: `results.json` (verdicts by `check_results.py`), the repository's results check, the results page, and `check_reproduction.py` against the committed outputs (`report.md`); `CHECK` fails the run if anything differs.

## Limits

- **The SAS code is lost and SAS is not available.** The fit is rebuilt from the paper's description of PROC NLMIXED and checked against direct numerical integration and the paper's tables, not against NLMIXED (`port` is not attempted).
- **Convergence is NLMIXED's.** Which fits count as converged decides the group-size-5 rows of Tables 1 and 3, Table 4's convergence and the low-convergence models of Table 5. Our optimizer follows NLMIXED's documented defaults; its line search and update are not public. Every summary depends on this through the fits it keeps.
- **Three readings were found from the tables**, not read from the paper: σ01 estimated, σ0 and σ1 as variances, and Table 5's non-coverage over all data sets (`found_by_search` in `results.json`). The follow-up's likelihood-ratio tests are a fourth.
- **Table 4's designs are not stated.** We pool the nine designs of the main grid; no subset reproduces the paper's convergence.
- **Monte Carlo error.** Every cell carries it, Table 5 most (100 data sets per cell).
readme.summary_prose:
Every simulated cell is compared at a tolerance fixed before the comparison: half a printed unit plus three
combined Monte Carlo standard errors ([figure-reproduction/README.md](figure-reproduction/README.md#comparing-monte-carlo-tables)).
No simulated item can be "exact": the paper gives no seeds, and three of its unstated settings were found by testing
against its tables.

**What came back.** {cells_within} of the {cells_total} printed cells of Tables 1-5 came back within Monte Carlo error.
In the 19 designs where 98-100% of fits converged, every bias and non-coverage cell of Tables 1 and 3 came back
({table1_stable_within} of 114 and {table3_stable_within} of 114), and so did Table 4's biases and non-coverage. The
pattern of convergence came back: fits fail with few small groups and a small random intercept.

**What did not.** Which fits count as converged is NLMIXED's verdict. Our NLMIXED-like optimizer converges in
{conv_30x5}% of data sets of 30 groups of 5 (paper 56, 68, 76), so the group-size-5 rows of Tables 1 and 3, Table 4's
convergence and the t3 models of Table 5 differ where they depend on which fits are kept. σ0's interval covers more
often than the paper's where the random intercept is small. Each gap has its tested hypotheses in `results.json`.

**Settings the paper does not state**, each tested against its tables (`output/comparison.json`, `hypotheses`):

- σ0 and σ1 are the variances as fitted, not standard deviations: the biases at group size 5 only come back on the
  variance scale, and so do the intervals ({ci_variance_stable} of {ci_stable_n} high-convergence σ cells of Table 3,
  against {ci_sd_scale_stable} on the SD scale).
- The model estimates σ01, although the data have none. Without it nearly every data set of groups of 5 converges.
- A fit also stops when no parameter moves by more than 1e-8 (the paper's "absolute parameter convergence
  criterion", NLMIXED's ABSXCONV); fits creeping towards a zero variance stop this way and count as converged.
- Table 5's non-coverage counts a data set that did not converge as not covered: {table5_noncoverage_within} of 432
  cells come back, against {h_table5_noncoverage_converged_only_table5_noncoverage} over converged fits only.

**Slips in the paper**, found by recomputing its text from its own tables (`text.arithmetic`): the Methods give
σ0 = 1.42 for a variance of 2.0 (√2 = 1.41); the text puts the largest γ01 and γ11 biases at 30 x 5, ICC 0.04,
where Table 1 has them at ICC 0.38 and 0.17; "1% or less" at 100 x 30, where Table 1 prints 1.04 and 1.07;
variance-component non-coverage of "7% to 17%" by cell, where Table 3 goes down to 0.030; the convergence of groups
of 5 (80.4%) is not the mean of Table 1's (81.1%); and "no significant difference between the rates of convergence"
with groups larger than 5, where Table 5 has model 4 at 76% against model 1's 100%. Table 2's σ0 row by ICC repeats
its row by number of groups but is what Table 3 gives: not a copy error.
